text:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu-x9 (eu-central-1) pool queue surged to ~12k sustained for 9m. Autoscaler attempted scale-ups but cloud returned 429/RateLimit and several 403/Quota errors. Pod eviction rate rising. Paging on-call.

Alex: I'm oncall. pinging @Maya @Li @Jamie @Priya. Initiating triage — what's the immediate customer impact?

Sam: CS: multiple orgs seeing 504s and spikes in generation latency, small customers first, but one enterprise (gamma-corp) reports degraded throughput on scheduled batch jobs. Opening incident tickets for affected customers.

Maya: grabbing metrics and driver logs. Can someone paste node statuses for gpu-x9 nodes?

Jamie: from the node pool logs (gpu-x9-node-04):
```
[2026-03-15T03:11:42Z] nvidia: Xid 79 (ECC error) on GPU0
[2026-03-15T03:11:43Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 45721 (python) total-vm:34G
[2026-03-15T03:11:44Z] kubelet: Evicting pods due to kernel memory pressure
[2026-03-15T03:11:45Z] kube-proxy: connection reset by peer
```
Jamie: multiple nodes show similar Xid/OOM signatures. We rolled a driver update v2.12 two days ago — possible regression.

Li: infra: autoscaler burst policy hit provider rate limits (429s) and we hit quota ceiling for new instance types in eu-central-1. Cloud ticket 123321 opened, but approval isn't immediate. I've temporarily disabled burst scaling for this pool.

Priya: ops suggestion: reduce per-pod concurrency and offload long-seq requests to quantized model (mini-q) and smaller instance types for warmup. Could also apply per-request sequence caps at the edge as quick mitigation.

Alex: agreed. Draft immediate mitigation steps:
1) Drain and cordon the most affected nodes in gpu-x9 to stop scheduling on hot nodes.
2) Rollback driver to v2.10 on a small canary set.
3) Disable autoscaler bursts and lower target buffer.
4) Route critical enterprise traffic to dedicated pool gpu-ded-1 (same region).
5) Edge filter to reject or downgrade requests with seq_len > 4096.
6) Notify CS with interim messaging and ETA.

Jamie: executing step 1 now.
```
kubectl cordon gpu-x9-n04 -n inference
kubectl drain gpu-x9-n04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
```
Jamie: initiating driver rollback on two canary nodes to v2.10. deploy-bot: please run rollback canary.

deploy-bot: acknowledged. rolling driver v2.12 -> v2.10 on nodes gpu-x9-n07,gpu-x9-n08. Estimated 4m.

Li: changed autoscaler policy: bursts disabled, target_buffer set to 15%. Also limited scale-up rate to 1 node per 90s to avoid further rate-limiting.

Maya: after cordons and policy change, queue dipped from ~12k -> ~5.2k in 6m. Error rate decreased from 18% -> 9%.

Sam: proposed CS blurb: "We're experiencing reduced GPU capacity in eu-central-1 due to node instability and provider quota limits. We're routing critical workloads to dedicated pools and applying temporary throttles; engineers are rolling back a recent driver update. We'll provide another update in 30 minutes." Approve?

Alex: send that. Add ETA: 30-40m for noticeable recovery.

Priya: canary results: driver v2.10 on gpu-x9-n07 shows no Xid/OOM for 8m, memory usage stable. Proceeding to roll to an additional 6 nodes but holding 3 nodes as standby for validation.

Priya: note — cross-pool routing caused increased latency for some enterprise customers because sticky session pins were broken. I'll implement sticky routing for dedicated pools to keep enterprise traffic on their pinned pools.

Li: cloud ops update: provider granted ephemeral +8 instances for eu-central-1 for 4 hours. Requested permanent quota increase.

Maya: root cause quick-find: a combination of very long-sequence batched requests (seq_len >= 3072) that expand KV cache and trigger large memory allocations under the new driver, leading to OOMs and Xid errors. Autoscaler thrash then exacerbated queue growth due to rate-limited scale-ups.

Alex: agreed follow-ups: enforce seq-length limits per plan, update autoscaler heuristics to consider free-GPU-memory, and run driver regression suite against long-seq workloads.

Jamie: immediate protective filter: edge will return 413 for seq_len > 8192 and will downgrade >4096 to mini-q. Pushing config now.

deploy-bot: edge rule deployed (id edge-20260315-09). Active in 20s.

Maya: metrics now: queue ~1.9k, overall error rate 2.7%, p99 latency improving but still elevated for a handful of enterprise routes.

Sam: CS notified affected customers with update. They asked for impact window and root-cause analysis in a postmortem.

Alex: severity S2. We will keep pager until full recovery and handoff a concise runbook to the night person.

Priya: finishing driver rollout to remaining nodes. Also flagging nodes with >2 Xid events in 1h for replacement and capturing kernel dumps to /s3/incidents/2234567800/dumps.

Maya: follow-ups list:
- full postmortem and timeline
- autoscaler change: include free-gpu-memory and sequence-profile heuristics
- permanent quota escalation with cloud ops
- edge request protections by customer tier
- driver regression tests for long-seq workloads

Alex: handoff note to @Maya: "gpu-x9 experienced a driver-induced memory regression causing Xid/OOM node flaps and autoscaler rate-limit thrash. Mitigations: cordon/drain bad nodes, rollback driver to v2.10, disabled bursts, edge sequence caps, routed critical traffic to gpu-ded-1, temporary quota +8. Current: stable with elevated p99 on a few hotspots; metrics trending good. Please own postmortem and follow-ups"

Maya: ack — I'll take it from here and file the postmortem. Great coordination. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Incident logged: INC-20260315-8801. Linked commits: revert/driver-20260309, edge-20260315-09.

Alex: closing on-call handover. Will reopen if we see regression. Last status check 03:54Z.
